title: All Four Quasideterminants
content: Defines the complete set of quasideterminants for a $2 \times 2$ matrix over a division ring $D$. Each is a Schur complement: $|A|_{00} = a - b d^{-1} c$, $|A|_{01} = b - a c^{-1} d$, $|A|_{10} = c - d b^{-1} a$, $|A|_{11} = d - c a^{-1} b$. Unlike CramersRuleOQ03.lean which defines only the two diagonal quasideterminants, this file provides all four, enabling the full algebraic theory.
mathContext: Each quasideterminant uses a different entry as pivot. The notation $|A|_{ij}$ means: take entry $a_{ij}$, subtract (rest of row $i$) $\cdot$ (complementary entry)$^{-1}$ $\cdot$ (rest of column $j$). In the $2 \times 2$ case, the 'complementary entry' is a single scalar.

title: Commutative Reduction: All Four Formulas
content: Over a commutative field $F$, each quasideterminant times its complementary diagonal entry equals $\pm\det(A)$: $|A|_{00} \cdot a_{11} = \det(A)$, $a_{00} \cdot |A|_{11} = \det(A)$, $|A|_{01} \cdot a_{10} = -\det(A)$, $a_{11} \cdot |A|_{10} = -\det(A)$. The sign pattern (positive for diagonal, negative for off-diagonal) mirrors the cofactor sign convention.
mathContext: In the commutative case, $|A|_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} \det(A) / a_{kl}$ where $(k,l)$ is the complementary position. This is the ratio of the full determinant to the complementary minor — the non-commutative version replaces this ratio with a Schur complement.

title: Row and Column Scaling Identities
content: Proves that quasideterminants are left-linear in their row and right-linear in their column: if row 0 is scaled by $\lambda$ from the left, $|A'|_{00} = \lambda \cdot |A|_{00}$; if column 0 is scaled by $\lambda$ from the right, $|A'|_{00} = |A|_{00} \cdot \lambda$. In non-commutative rings, left and right scaling are distinct, so both identities are needed.
mathContext: The scaling identity $|\lambda \cdot \text{row}_i(A)|_{ij} = \lambda \cdot |A|_{ij}$ is the non-commutative analogue of $\det(\lambda \cdot \text{row}_i(A)) = \lambda \cdot \det(A)$. The proof uses `mul_sub` and associativity.

title: Alternate Non-Commutative Cramer's Rule
content: Proves `nc_cramers_rule_alt`: $A \cdot \text{ncSolveAlt}(A, b) = b$ using $|A|_{11}$ instead of $|A|_{00}$. The alternate formula pivots on $a_{00}$: $x_1 = |A|_{11}^{-1}(b_1 - a_{10} a_{00}^{-1} b_0)$, $x_0 = a_{00}^{-1}(b_0 - a_{01} x_1)$. Together with OQ-03's result, this covers all invertible $2 \times 2$ matrices: use OQ-03 when $a_{11} \neq 0$, this when $a_{00} \neq 0$.
mathContext: Every invertible $2 \times 2$ matrix over a division ring has at least one nonzero diagonal entry (otherwise both rows would start/end with zero, contradicting invertibility). The two pivoting strategies provide complete coverage.

title: Schur Complement Matrix Inversion
content: Defines the explicit matrix inverse $A^{-1}$ via the quasideterminant. Entry $(0,0)$ is $|A|_{00}^{-1}$, entry $(1,0)$ is $-d^{-1} c |A|_{00}^{-1}$, etc. Proves two of the four verification entries: $A \cdot A^{-1}$ has $(0,0) = 1$ and $(1,0) = 0$. Both use the factoring pattern $(a - b d^{-1} c) \cdot q^{-1} = q \cdot q^{-1} = 1$.
mathContext: The Schur complement inversion formula is the $2 \times 2$ scalar case of the general block matrix inversion lemma, which is fundamental in numerical linear algebra, Kalman filtering, and the Woodbury identity.

title: Proportionality of Diagonal Quasideterminants
content: Over a commutative field, the two diagonal quasideterminants satisfy $|A|_{00} \cdot a_{11} = a_{00} \cdot |A|_{11}$ (both equal $\det(A)$). Equivalently, $|A|_{00} = \det(A) / a_{11}$ and $|A|_{11} = \det(A) / a_{00}$. This proportionality fails in the non-commutative case, where the two quasideterminants are genuinely independent objects.
mathContext: The failure of proportionality in the non-commutative case means that a $2 \times 2$ matrix over a division ring genuinely needs two quasideterminants to describe its invertibility, not just one determinant. This is why the Gelfand-Retakh theory introduces $n^2$ quasideterminants for $n \times n$ matrices.
